searchText: > Stateless clients need to be able to expose and serve the JSON-RPC API. > Stateless clients need to be able to participate in transaction gossip even when they don’t have any of the state. In your article you have those two as AND requirements. I contend that there is value even if they are OR requirements. I think if stateless clients could gossip, but not serve JSON-RPC that is valuable. I also think that if stateless clients could serve JSON-RPC but not gossip that is also valuable. Right now we have *many* users who *neither* gossip *nor* handle their own JSON-RPC (everyone who uses infura/alchemy). Either getting some of those users participating in gossip, or getting some of those users serving their own JSON-RPC requests would be an improvement over the current situation. worth noting that `eth_sendTransaction` depends on gossip so there's some interdependency between these things And JSON-RPC drops very quickly in usefulness when you start removing endpoints. I started writing this document this morning to try and both - document all the various moving parts that go into eth1 clients, ideas for client functionality, stateless stuff, etc - document the interplay between various features and functionality https://notes.ethereum.org/hKVy2i8gSYSh8BbHV16g9Q?view I'll look into transferring this into something that is more "wiki" like so that it can be more collaboratively edited.
